headline: Brazil maintains Selic rate at 13.75% as inflation concerns persist
summary: The Brazilian Central Bank's Copom committee held the Selic interest rate at 13.75%. Analysts suggest the rate may remain elevated through the end of the year due to a deteriorating inflation outlook.
why: The Selic rate is the primary tool for managing inflation in Brazil. High rates attract foreign capital but increase the cost of debt for the government and domestic companies.
why_moved: The decision to hold rates despite market expectations for cuts influences yield curves and currency flows, as investors adjust their carry trade strategies.
